The test image shows a soybean leaf with small, scattered reddish-brown spots distributed across the leaf surface. The spots are small, roughly circular to irregular, without obvious yellow halos or gray centers. The leaf is otherwise green and healthy-looking.

Top candidates: Septoria_brown_spot (small scattered brown spots), Soybean_rust (small brown pustules), Bacterial_Pustule (small spots).

Let me check one reference image.

The Septoria reference shows advanced yellowing with dark brown spots on yellowed tissue — the test image doesn't match (leaf is fully green, spots are smaller/scattered).

The test image appears to show the underside of a green soybean leaf with small scattered reddish-brown spots. This pattern — small discrete brown lesions scattered across an otherwise green leaf — is more consistent with Soybean rust (small uredinia/pustules on leaf surface) or early Septoria.

The spots in the test image are small, reddish-brown, scattered without yellow halos or angular shape. Rust typically presents as tiny brown spots/pustules on the underside of leaves, which matches the leaf orientation and spot characteristics here.
